topics.headline: Title III FY 2026-27 RFAs are live — the window to shape allowable use starts now
topics.why_matters: Five active partners (Ocean Grove, South Sutter, Visions, Heartland, Pacific Coast Academy) have confirmed Title III Immigrant receipts, and 18 partners have never applied — Danielle's outreach angle. Plus the Title III allocation came in at $890 million, unchanged from the previous fiscal year, even as the EL student population continues to grow. Scarcity + open application window = urgency post.
topics.angle: "The Title III 2026-27 RFA is open. Here's what allowable use looks like for supplemental EL intervention in an independent-study charter — and what it doesn't cover."
topics.roman_take: Flat federal EL funding into a growing EL population is a math problem the field keeps pretending is a policy problem. If your Title III dollars are supplemental by law, the question isn't "should we tutor" — it's "why aren't we already."
topics.danielle_take: Walk through the actual RFA line items and what a defensible Title III-funded intervention plan looks like — sessions per week, tutor qualifications, evidence tier documentation — so a special programs coordinator can build their application against a real spec instead of a template. ---

topics.headline: The Oct 15 double-release — Dashboard + CAASPP land on the same day for the first time
topics.category: B (with C spillover — every Tier A partner is affected)
topics.why_matters: Every partner — Visions, iLEAD, Ocean Grove, South Sutter, Sky Mountain, Heartland, Compass, Pacific Coast Academy, all of them — will get hit with assessment results and Dashboard color changes on the same October morning. Making assessment and accountability information available at the same time means charter directors lose the traditional gap week to prep messaging. They will need proof points fast. This is exactly the moment A+'s case study data (LTEL reclassification lifts, MAP Growth gains) becomes the argument that the number on the Dashboard is not the whole story.
topics.angle: "October 15 is the new stress test for California charters. Here's what to have ready before Dashboard + CAASPP land the same day." Frame A+ as the operational partner that shows up in the intervention data behind the accountability numbers.
topics.roman_take: Conviction angle — the aligned release exposes a truth the sector has avoided: schools have been managing two narratives (assessment vs. accountability) and now have to tell one. Only schools with real intervention data can.
topics.danielle_take: Implementation angle — a 6-week checklist for special programs coordinators: pull last year's CAASPP by subgroup, cross-reference with intervention hours logged, identify the 3 subgroups where you need talking points ready by Oct 16.

topics.headline: Varsity Tutors for Schools shut down — and cited a lack of evidence
topics.why_matters: This is the strongest competitive intel signal of the year. Varsity Tutors for Schools saw a steep decline in business as pandemic aid ran out and districts demanded more proof of learning gains for students. The post-pandemic tutoring market is entering a more difficult phase as school districts move beyond the temporary federal funding that helped fuel a rapid expansion of academic interventions. At the end of July, Varsity Tutors told its school customers that it would discontinue its Varsity for Schools services, effective immediately. In a shareholder letter, the company said the decision would allow it to shift its focus and resources back to its original model as a consumer tutoring business. The exit hit A+'s territory directly: Antelope Valley Union High School District's $1,499,900 agreement ran through May 31, 2026, before the shutdown. (Note: Antelope Valley Union HSD is a traditional district, not A+'s Tier A iLEAD Antelope Valley — but the geographic and cultural adjacency is real, and iLEAD leadership will have seen this story.)
topics.angle: "The scale players are exiting K-12. The partnership players are still here. Here's what changed and what it means for the charters we serve." Cite the shareholder letter + The 74 evidence framing.
topics.roman_take: The conviction angle — Cohn estimated that Nerdy's revenue for this year would drop by $12 million to $15 million because of the shutdown of its district work is what happens when you treat schools as a growth channel instead of a partnership. A+ never optimized for scale over trust and this is the payoff.
topics.danielle_take: The implementation angle — with a $1.5M Antelope Valley contract disappearing mid-year, dozens of school leaders in Southern California are staring at a Q4 hole. What she'd tell a director who just lost their tutoring vendor 4 weeks into the school year (pull from the iEM playbook). ---
